subject: maths
title: Surface area of prisms and cylinders

lines.say: Surface area is the total area of all the outside faces of a solid.
Think of wrapping a present. You cover every face.
Unfold the solid flat and you get a net. It shows every face.
lines.alt: Net of a rectangular prism with base, front, back, top and two sides

lines.say: Surface area is in square units, like centimetres squared.
A box 8 by 5 by 3 centimetres has three pairs of matching faces.
Top and bottom are 8 by 5. That's 2 times 40, which is 80.

draw.alt: Three pairs of faces: 8 by 5, 8 by 3 and 5 by 3

lines.say: Front and back are 8 by 3, so 48. The two ends are 5 by 3, so 30.
Add all six faces. 80 plus 48 plus 30 is 158.
A prism has two identical ends, and rectangles wrap around the sides.
The band's length is the perimeter of the end.
This triangular prism has a right-angled triangle end. 6, 8 and 10 centimetres.
lines.alt: Triangular prism with end sides 6 cm, 8 cm and 10 cm and length 12 cm

lines.say: Each triangle is a half times 6 times 8, which is 24. Two ends make 48.
The perimeter is 24. Times the length 12 gives 288.
So the surface area is 336 square centimetres.
A cylinder is like two coins and a label.
The label wraps around the circle, so its length is the circumference, 2 pi r.

draw.alt: The label's length is marked 2πr and its height h

lines.say: So a closed cylinder is two circles plus the curved surface.
Radius 4, height 10. 32 pi plus 80 pi is 112 pi.
A tank with no lid has only one circle.
Radius 0.5 metres, height 1.2 metres. Leave out the top circle.

draw.alt: The lid circle is crossed out

lines.say: The base is 0.25 pi. The curved part is 1.2 pi.
That's about 4.56 square metres of metal.
A closed prism has two ends. Count both.
Check for open, no lid, or open-topped.
Use the radius, not the diameter. Halve the diameter first.
Triangles need the half. A half times base times height.
Surface area is squared units. Volume is cubed.
Unfold it flat. Surface area is the area of the net.
Two ends, then wrap the band.
Cylinder. Two coins and a label.
Check the lid before you finish.
